_header: Extra header fields after the four fixed integers (magic, version, format digest, kernel schema, compiler identity), in declaration order. `string` is length-prefixed UTF-8. `app_id` is the app identity, reverse-DNS (LLP 1023 D5): bake writes it from DataSource::app_id(); empty is unnamed (a fixture or a stand-in) and unnamed matches anything at boot. LLP 1038 D2: router names the root slot filled before initializers.

header.name: locale
header._comment: @ref LLP 1060 D4: the root string slot holding the resolved locale every `t(...)` reads; set only when the app calls `t`. The runner writes it from set_place.

_about: The single declaration authority for the plan: its tables, the expression VM's opcodes, the stdlib roster, and the enum vocabularies. plan/build.rs generates the row structs, the canonical encoder, the validating decoder, the opcode and stdlib enums, and FORMAT_DIGEST from this file. Nothing here is hand-mirrored anywhere else. Kernel node types, props, and style rows are NOT declared here: plan rows carry the kernel's ordinals as numbers, and the crates that give them meaning take the vocabulary from exact-kernel (LLP 1004 D2).
_codecs: u8 | u16 | u32 | i32 | f64 | bool | str (u32 index into the string pool) | enum:<Name> (u8 ordinal) | idx:<table> (u32 row index, validated) | opt:<table> (u32 row index or NONE = 0xFFFFFFFF) | range:<table> (u32 start + u32 len, validated) | code (u32 offset + u32 len into the code pool, validated as well-formed bytecode) | bytes (u32 offset + u32 len into the data pool)
_tables: Document order is significant: nodes and regions with the same parent are ordered by `order`; an arm's content is every node and region whose `arm` names it; a node with no parent inside an arm is one of the arm's roots. Fonts are static in v1: a face is exactly one source path, weight, and italic flag. Variable-axis ranges are additive later, never inferred from the file by a host.

fields.name: owner
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1017.000 (child state): the arm whose instance owns this slot — an `each` row, a `when` or `match` arm. The slot is created, its init evaluated in that arm's frames, when the arm instance is created, and dropped with it. None: a root slot.

fields.name: late
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1017.000 (child state): a root slot holding the state of a child used outside every region; its init runs once at the boot render, after boot settlement (so it may read derives and resources), not with the other root slots before it. Always false when owner is set.

fields.name: context
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1027.005 D6: trailing request-context argument count; 0 without `with`. Only persisted kept-answer admission compares the identifying prefix. All live requests, compiled values, carry and document checkpoints compare every argument. Must not exceed args.len.

fields.name: placeholder
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1048.003 D6: the row whose value shows while this one's source hasn't answered and nothing is kept for its arguments — a declared `else source(args)`, compiled as a row of its own (named `<name>#else`, arguments that read no state, the same type, no placeholder of its own). None: a list or an option shows its empty value, and anything else has none.

fields.name: placeholder_value
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1054.000.002 D3: a declared `else empty(field=value, …)`, the compiler's constant (a value), shown while nothing is kept and the source has not answered. Empty bytes: none — an undeclared placeholder is the type's zero, which the runner computes (D1).

fields.name: refreshes
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1054.000.000 D1: the resources a send to this mutation refreshes, forced, when it runs and when its reply lands (`mutation m as shape T refreshes a, b`).

fields.name: then
fields._comment: The action a `mutation … then action` runs after each answer lands, as its own commit (LLP 1016.001). None: nothing runs.

fields.name: queue
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1092 D1, D2: `mutation m as shape T queue` — one send in flight; a later send waits, with its send-time arguments, until the one before it is answered or let go and its `then` has run. False: the newest send wins (LLP 1016 §4).

fields.name: name
fields._comment: The task's name, for the agent's `state.tasks` (LLP 1092 D10).

fields.name: gated
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1092 D7, D8: `task t when cond`: the timer is armed while `gate` is true and idle (an infinite deadline) while it is false. False: `mount`, armed from boot.

fields.name: gate
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1092 D9: the gate, a bool, evaluated at each commit after its settlement; the constant `true` for an ungated task.

fields.name: keyed
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1092 D7, D8: `key=expr`: a changed key (compared as an `each` key is) re-arms the timer from the commit's time.

fields.name: key
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1092 D9: the key, a string, number or bool; the constant `true` when not keyed.

fields.name: render
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1048 D2, LLP 1048.003 D5: when the route's document renders; undeclared is client.

fields.name: activate
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1048.003 D5: when a rendered page's runtime loads; inferred when undeclared.

fields.name: paint
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1048.005: what a served page's reader sees first; `settled` (undeclared) is the settled page, `boot` the boot document, sent before any answer, then the settled page.

fields.name: pages
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1048.000 D2, LLP 1048.003 D5: the source that lists a parameterized route's pages — the values of its one parameter, a list<string> — for the build to render and the server's sitemap to name. Empty: none.

fields.name: pages_args
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1048.000 D2: that source's arguments, values (a list in the plan's value encoding); empty bytes without a source.

tables.name: keyframes
tables._comment: @ref LLP 1055 D5: the app's `@keyframes` rules by name, each body as CSS text (`0%{r:3px;}100%{r:9px;}`); the runner resolves `animation-name` against them.

tables.name: sounds
tables._comment: @ref LLP 1096 D1: each declared sound, a WAV the compiler read: its app-relative path (what `playSound` names), its length in frames at its own rate, its channels, and the SHA-256 of its bytes as hex. The runner reads a voice's natural length, frames / rate; the hosts read which files to decode.

tables.name: profiles
tables._comment: @ref LLP 1100 D3: the app's `@color-profile`s by name: the ICC file (an asset path) and the rendering intent; `color(--name …)` resolves against them, and the platform draws it.

tables.name: hatches
tables._comment: @ref LLP 1075.003.000.001 §4.3: each hatch word app.json declares, with the platforms whose module handles it as a mask (bit 0 ios, 1 tvos, 2 macos, 3 web, 4 linux, 5 windows, 6 android; a plain list is every bit). A host calls a word only where its bit is set, so a platform taken off a word stops being called with the next bundle.

tables.name: texts
tables._comment: @ref LLP 1060 D3: one localized text, `{name}` placeholders unfilled. Within a locale, sorted by key.

tables.name: locales
tables._comment: @ref LLP 1060 D3: one strings table per locale (BCP 47 name). Row 0 is the base; the rest are in name order. rtl is the CLDR script direction, compiled once. Table names remain for data-only strings. Only the keys the app's `t` calls name.

_enums: Wire ordinal is the 0-based index. An unknown ordinal is a typed decode rejection.
_opcodes: The expression VM: a stack machine over values with a small locals stack (`BindLocal` pops into it, `LoadLocal` copies from it, `DropLocal` pops it) for names an inline `match` binds and the item and index a `Map`/`Filter` callback binds. Each opcode names its operand layout; the decoder validates framing and every index operand. `depth` operands count enclosing instance scopes (0 = innermost). Type inference guarantees stack discipline; the VM still traps, never UB.

opcodes.name: LoadIndex
opcodes._comment: LLP 1062 D8: the position (a number from 0) of the `each` row `depth` scopes out, as `each item, i in list` names it.

opcodes.name: Map
opcodes._comment: @ref LLP 1017.003 D5: pops a list; runs the callback body that follows inline up to the operand's offset once per item, with the item and its index bound as the next two locals; pushes the list of the values the body leaves.

opcodes.name: Filter
opcodes._comment: @ref LLP 1017.003 D5: as `Map`, keeping each item whose body leaves `true`.

_stdlib: The enumerated roster (LLP 1004 D2/D4): every callable an expression may name, with its parameter types and return type (`any` = one of number, string, bool, list). The compiler checks calls against this table; the runner's VM implements each entry once; entries are added by fixture, never by speculation. LLP 1038 D3: Router and Entry name reserved record shapes; list<Router>, list<Entry>, and list<string> are typed lists.

stdlib.name: performanceNow
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1109 D1: the web's `performance.now()`: milliseconds on the runner's monotonic clock since boot (the driver's clock under the agent, from 0), not the date. Renamed from `now()`, which is refused (`type-now-renamed`).

stdlib.name: formatTime
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1054.000.003 D1/D7: `h:mm AM` of (epochMs, utcOffset minutes east), as Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { timeZone: <the offset>, timeStyle: "short" }) prints it. Core: every app links it, as it linked formatClockTime. A parameter spelled as string literals (`"a" | "b"`) is a string the compiler requires written as one of them.

stdlib.name: includes
stdlib._comment: The web's `String.prototype.includes(needle)`: a case-sensitive literal substring search; the empty needle matches. @ref LLP 1088 §9.1: over a list of strings, numbers or bools, `Array.prototype.includes(item)` (SameValueZero: NaN is NaN, -0 is 0), one list step per item scanned up to the match. `any` is the type checker's. The web's optional position argument is not taken.

stdlib.name: trim
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1054.000.005 D1: JavaScript's String.prototype.trim — ECMA-262 WhiteSpace and LineTerminator, not Rust's White_Space.

stdlib.name: first
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1054.000 C4: a list's first item, `some(x)`, or `none` for an empty list; `any` is `list<T>` in and `option<T>` out (the type checker's).

stdlib.name: t
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1060 D2: the text for (locale, key), placeholders filled from name/value pairs. The compiler writes every argument; an author writes `t("key", name=value)`.

stdlib.name: map
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1017.003 D4: `map(list<T>, (T, number) => U) -> list<U>` (the type checker's). Lowered to the `Map` opcode, never `Call`: the row reserves the name.

stdlib.name: filter
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1017.003 D4: `filter(list<T>, (T, number) => bool) -> list<T>`. Lowered to the `Filter` opcode, never `Call`.

stdlib.name: join
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1017.003 D4: the web's `Array.prototype.join` over a list of strings, numbers or bools, each printed as `toString` prints it.

stdlib.name: formatDate
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1054.000.003 D2/D7/D8: the calendar date of (epochMs, utcOffset), as Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US") prints it: `medium` is { dateStyle: "medium" }, `month-year` is { month: "long", year: "numeric" }. @ref LLP 1102 §3.4: `iso` is `YYYY-MM-DD`, the date at that wall time: `Date.prototype.toISOString`'s date part at a whole-minute offset (a fractional offset's wall time is not clipped to a millisecond again, as no style's is); outside years 1–9999 it prints `""`, as every style does (D7). The linked capability `format`.

stdlib.name: formatNumber
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1054.000.003 D3/D7/D8: Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", { notation: "compact", roundingMode: "trunc", signDisplay: "negative" }). The linked capability `format`.

stdlib.name: frame
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1051.000 D1/D2: where layout put the first node whose `id` prop is the argument, as last laid out: its border box in its root's space, free of transforms and scrolling. Actions only (the compiler refuses it elsewhere).

stdlib.name: measure
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1051.000 D1/D2: the node's border box as if its `height` were `auto`, under the offer it has now. Actions only; the id is a string literal, so the runner answers it before the action runs.

stdlib.name: at
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1006 §3: JavaScript's Array.prototype.at — `some` of the item at an index truncated toward zero, counted from the end when negative, `none` past either end; `any` is `list<T>` in and `option<T>` out (the type checker's).

stdlib.name: startsWith
stdlib._comment: The web's `String.prototype.startsWith(prefix)`: whether the text begins with the prefix, case-sensitive; the empty prefix matches. The web's optional position argument is not taken.

stdlib.name: endsWith
stdlib._comment: The web's `String.prototype.endsWith(suffix)`: whether the text ends with the suffix, case-sensitive; the empty suffix matches. The web's optional end-position argument is not taken.

stdlib.name: slice
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1088 D2: JavaScript's `String.prototype.slice(start, end?)` over UTF-16 code units (ToIntegerOrInfinity: NaN is 0, fractions truncate, a negative index counts from the end, both clamped); an omitted `end` is `Number.MAX_VALUE`, which clamps as `undefined` does (a plan's constants are finite, so not `Infinity`). The result is made well formed: a lone surrogate half becomes U+FFFD. @ref LLP 1088 §9.1: over a list, `Array.prototype.slice(start, end?)` by the same clamp, one list step per item kept, the result's extent checked as a `List` is; `any` is `string` or `list<T>` in and the same out (the type checker's).

stdlib.name: replaceAll
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1088 D2: JavaScript's `String.prototype.replaceAll(find, with)` with a string `find`: every match, left to right, `GetSubstitution` applied (`$$`, `$&`, `` $` ``, `$'`; `$1` is literal), an empty `find` inserting at every code-unit boundary; the whole result made well formed once, and bounded by `MAX_STRING` UTF-8 bytes as it is built.

stdlib.name: toLowerCase
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1088 D2: JavaScript's `String.prototype.toLowerCase()`: Unicode's default, locale-independent mapping with final sigma. Linked by use: it reaches the kernel's case tables through `text-transform`'s link (capability `text_transform`), bounded by `MAX_STRING`.

stdlib.name: concat
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1088 §9.1: JavaScript's `Array.prototype.concat(other)` of two lists of one item type, `list<T>, list<T> -> list<T>` (the type checker's): one list step per item of the result, taken before it is built, then its extent checked as a `List` is (LLP 1090 D3).

stdlib.name: indexOf
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1088 §9.1 (2026-10-04 note): JavaScript's `String.prototype.indexOf(needle)` — the first match's position in UTF-16 code units, `-1` for none, 0 for the empty needle — or, over a list of strings, numbers or bools, `Array.prototype.indexOf(item)` by IsStrictlyEqual (NaN is never found, -0 is 0), one list step per item scanned up to the match. `any` is the type checker's. The web's optional position argument is not taken.

stdlib.name: split
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1088 §9.1 (2026-10-04 note): JavaScript's `String.prototype.split(separator)` with a string separator: the pieces between its matches, left to right; an empty separator splits into UTF-16 code units (each piece made well formed: a lone half is U+FFFD), and `""` into no pieces. One list step per piece, taken before the list is built, then its extent checked as a `List` is (LLP 1090 D3). The web's limit argument and regular expressions are not taken.

stdlib.name: elementFromPoint
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1094 D10: DOM's `document.elementFromPoint(x, y)?.closest("[id]")?.id` over `frame`'s boxes: the `id` of the front-most laid-out box at the viewport point (every scroll applied, no transforms; ancestors' overflow clips; `pointer-events: none`, `display: none` and `visibility: hidden` skipped; LLP 1083.000's paint order), or of its nearest ancestor with one; `none` where no box or ancestor has one. Actions only.

stdlib.name: parseNumber
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1102 §3.1: a decimal number in text, `some(n)`, else `none`. Surrounding whitespace is `trim`'s; then an optional sign, digits with an optional fraction or a fraction alone (`.5`; `5.` is 5), and an optional decimal exponent (`1e3`); nothing else (`""`, hex, `Infinity`, `NaN`, `12px` are `none`). The value is the correctly rounded double, as `Number()` reads it; a result past the largest finite is `none`, as is a nonzero numeral that rounds to zero; `-0` is -0.

stdlib.name: ceil
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1102 §3.2: JavaScript's `Math.ceil`, IEEE's ceiling (`ceil(-0.5)` is -0; NaN and the infinities are their own).

stdlib.name: round
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1102 §3.2: JavaScript's `Math.round`: the nearest integer, a tie toward +∞ (`round(-1.5)` is -1, `round(2.5)` is 3), and -0 for a negative input that rounds to zero (`round(-0.4)` is -0); NaN and the infinities are their own. Not Rust's `f64::round`, which breaks a tie away from zero.

stdlib.name: calendarDiff
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1102 §0, §3.4: the whole calendar years or months from the first ISO date (`YYYY-MM-DD`, proleptic Gregorian, years 0 through 9999) to the second, counted as an age is: a period completes when the later date's month and day reach the earlier date's (years compare month then day, months compare the day), so a Feb 29 start completes a year on Mar 1 of a common year and a Jan 31 start completes a month on Mar 1, as the web's `Temporal.PlainDate.prototype.until` counts with `largestUnit` `"years"` or `"months"` (date-fns' `differenceInMonths` differs: it lets a month's last day complete a month). When the second date is earlier, the count from it to the first, negated. `none` when either is not a valid `YYYY-MM-DD` date.

stdlib.name: toFixed
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1102 §0, §3.2 (decided (c)): JavaScript's `Number.prototype.toFixed(digits)`, the binary value rounded (`toFixed(1.005, 2)` is `"1.00"`, a tie away from zero on the exact value), `-0.001` at 2 is `"-0.00"`, a magnitude of `1e21` or more printed as `toString` prints it. One declared difference: a non-finite number prints `""` (LLP 1054.000.003 D7), where JavaScript prints `NaN` or `Infinity`. `digits` is a whole-number literal from 0 to 100, JavaScript's range. A linked `format` entry.

stdlib.name: formatDecimal
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1102 §0, §3.2 (decided (c)): an integer count of a smallest unit as a decimal with `digits` places, exactly (`formatDecimal(1234, 2)` is `"12.34"`, `formatDecimal(-5, 2)` is `"-0.05"`, `formatDecimal(7, 0)` is `"7"`); `-0` prints as `0`. A count that is not an integer, or not finite, prints `""`: money is a count of cents, or `formatDecimal(round(price * 100), 2)` for a price of at most two decimals under a trillion. `digits` is a whole-number literal from 0 to 20. A linked `format` entry.

_sources: LLP 1027 D2: the data seam's signatures. One row per data-source name the app's `resource` and `send` declarations use, with the parameter types and the result type every use agrees on (the compiler refuses a disagreement by name). An executor that marshals by shape — the TypeScript module's — reads this table at bind; a Rust crate ignores it. formatVersion 3.
_resources: `reader` (formatVersion 4, LLP 1027 D4 as ruled 2026-09-03): the bake found this resource consulting the store. Its `initial` is then the empty-store answer — the fresh install's first frame, never a developer's session (the bake's store is empty by construction, LLP 1018 D4) — and the runner treats it as a placeholder: a kept answer from the device's store beats it, and a data source that is not ready at boot (a TypeScript module before its host loads it) is asked again at `data_ready`. LLP 1038 D5: initial_args is a canonical Value::List of evaluated bake arguments, empty bytes only without a compiled value; initial is reused only for equal arguments. LLP 1027.005 D6: context is the trailing request-context count (0 without `with`), bounded by args.len. The persisted kept entry stores only the identifying prefix; only its admission while the source is unready compares that prefix. Every live request, compiled value, carry and document checkpoint still compares the full arguments.
